# Roudio build plan (10 Oct 2026)

How we go from designs to a working app. Each milestone ends with something
you can use on your own phone and recorder, plus a "done when" check. Build
in order. Each milestone relies on the ones before it.

Sources of truth:
- `docs/architecture/decisions.md`: what's decided and why (1–16).
- `docs/architecture/spec.md`: how it works (life of a recording, data, rules).
- `docs/design/`: screens (Paper file + `exports/`), flows, states, the
  inventory and the colour/dark mapping.

New screens will turn up during the build. Design them in Paper in the same
style, add them to `docs/design/screen-inventory.md`, and carry on.

## Repository layout

```
apps/
  android/        Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (Gradle)
  web/            React + TypeScript + Vite
services/
  backend/        Python: FastAPI api + worker (one package, two entry points)
packages/
  design-tokens/  tokens.json from Paper, generated into Compose theme + CSS variables
  api-spec/       openapi.json (generated by the backend), client generation scripts
docs/             brief, design, architecture, build
```

## Prerequisites (owner)

- Plaud developer portal: the **Android SDK files** and the
  `client_id` / `client_secret`.
- ElevenLabs API key (Creator plan to start).
- OpenAI API key with access to `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- A Google Cloud project with:
  - an OAuth client for **Android**, one for **web**, and one for the
    **backend**
  - the Drive API enabled with the `drive.file` scope (Roudio only sees
    files it creates)
- A Railway account.
- The phone, the Note Pro, and a USB cable for installing debug builds.

Keys go into Railway variables and local `.env` files that git ignores.
Never commit them.

## Milestone 0: Foundations

- Monorepo, linting, formatting, and CI that builds all three apps on every
  push.
- **Railway project:**
  - `api` and `worker` services
  - Postgres
  - a bucket
  - staging and production environments
- **Design tokens:** exported from Paper into `packages/design-tokens`, then
  generated into the Compose theme (light + dark) and CSS variables.
  Lexend is bundled in both apps.
- **Backend skeleton:**
  - health check
  - an OpenAPI description, with clients generated for web and Android
  - database migrations
  - the job table with a worker loop
- **Sign-in:**
  - Google sign-in on Android and web.
  - The backend checks the Google ID token, allows only the owner's email,
    and issues its own session.
  - The Drive grant (`drive.file`, offline) is stored encrypted for server
    uploads.
- **Plaud token:** `POST /plaud/token` exchanges `client_id`/`secret` for
  the SDK user token. The secret stays on the server.

**Done when:** you can sign in on the phone and on the web as yourself, any
other Google account is refused, and CI is green.

## Milestone 1: Linking the recorder (Android)

- `RecorderSource` interface, with its Plaud SDK implementation behind it.
- **Setup flow 11a–11i:**
  - welcome, sign-in, permissions, background exemptions (detecting Xiaomi
    autostart/battery state where Android allows), unlink from the Plaud app
  - find, choose, link, linked
- **Error screens 12a–12e:** each one triggered by the real SDK or Android
  condition.
- **Foreground service** (connected-device type) that holds the connection.
  It reads battery, storage, charging and recording-state events.
- **Recorder screen:** 13a (connected) and 13b (disconnected / unknown).
- The recorder chip on Today. It shows "unknown" when there's no fresh event.

**Done when:** a fresh install links to your Note Pro, the recorder screen
shows live battery and recording state, and turning Bluetooth off or walking
away shows the right screens.

## Milestone 2: Transfer, local store, upload queue

- **Export each finished recording:**
  - exported as Opus, then a SHA-256 checksum
  - Room database rows for the recording and its four track states
  - interrupted transfers restart from the beginning (decision 14)
  - Wi-Fi fast transfer for long files when it's available
- **Upload queue** (WorkManager):
  - resumable, chunked upload to the backend
  - the backend checks the checksum and stores the file in the bucket
- **Today** (phone) built for real: dial, timeline rows with the separate
  processing / backup words, the no-internet banner (S2), and the past-day
  view.
- **Measure:** Bluetooth vs Wi-Fi speed, and battery cost over a full day.
  Record the results in `docs/build/measurements.md`.
- **Firmware update gate:** only offered when every recording has reached
  "uploaded".

**Done when:** a day of recordings arrives on the server without you
touching the phone, a pulled plug or lost Bluetooth recovers by itself, and
nothing is ever deleted from the recorder.

## Milestone 3: Processing pipeline

- **Speech detector:** FireRedVAD runs over the original audio and stores
  speech segments with their offsets. The **tuning tool** (spec §5) comes
  first: run one real day, list what was kept and dropped, and listen to
  dropped samples. Settle the thresholds before going further.
- **Transcription** with Scribe v2:
  - speaker labels and keyterms from the word list
  - word timestamps mapped back to the original file
  - cost per recording logged
- **Tidy pass** (GPT-6.1 Sol): corrections stored as flagged edits, with
  the original kept.
- **Understand:**
  - group into conversations and events
  - title, summary, decisions and suggested tasks, each pointing at its
    source segments
- **Daily digest:** "updating" while recordings are still processing,
  "finished" after the day ends; quiet-day and failed states.
- **Sync down to the phone.** Screens:
  - Recording Notes / Transcript, including the "still writing up" and
    "writing up failed" states
  - player and chapters
- **Ask a recording:** answers with citations that the server checks, and
  the "not enough in this recording" answer.

**Done when:** a real conversation becomes a transcript with speaker labels
and a summary within about 15 minutes of upload, every summary point jumps
to the right moment, and Ask refuses to answer from outside the recording.

## Milestone 4: Drive backup and clean-up

- Drive uploads into a per-day folder: audio, transcript text + JSON, and
  notes/summary. Verified by MD5 and by reading the file back.
- **The clean-up gate** (spec §8): a recording is deleted from the recorder
  only when phone, server and Drive all match. The phone never deletes
  anything by itself.
- **Screens:**
  - Backups 14
  - Updates (03, 03b), with notification events for every failure and the
    way to recover
  - Recording More menu, delete-from-phone sheet, only-on-Drive state
- A "deleting turned off" safety switch, kept on until the gate has been
  watched for a week.

**Done when:** you've watched recordings clear from the recorder only after
their Drive copy was checked, and a Drive failure blocks clean-up and says
what's safe.

## Milestone 5: Search, Review, edits, word list

- **Search:**
  - full text in Postgres when online, SQLite FTS on the phone offline
  - results grouped by recording, with match type and time
  - no-results and offline states
- **Review:** waiting / accepted / done, the edit sheet, and "all caught up".
- **Transcript editing and speaker rename.** Edits sync up, and the latest
  edit wins per field.
- **Word list:** manual entries, words learned from repeated fixes (to
  confirm), and sending it to Scribe.
- **Settings 15–15c**, including the warning when a background exemption is
  switched off.

**Done when:** you can find any phrase from the last week in under two
seconds, offline too, and corrections you make start showing up correctly in
new recordings.

## Milestone 6: Web app

- Same API, same tokens. Screens:
  - W1 Sign in
  - W2 Today
  - W3/W3b Recording workspace with Ask
  - W4 Search
  - W5 Review
  - W6 Digest
  - W7 Updates
  - W8 Backups
  - W9 Settings
  - W10 narrow layout
- Audio streams from the backend copy.
- Keyboard shortcuts as designed.

**Done when:** everything you can read, search, ask and review on the phone
also works on the web, and the recorder status is honestly worded as "seen
by your phone".

## Milestone 7: Hardening

- Dark mode checked on every screen (token mapping), plus reduce motion and
  reduce transparency (solid fallbacks).
- **Accessibility:**
  - 200% font
  - 48 dp touch targets
  - TalkBack labels and reading order
  - 3-button navigation
  - keyboard insets
- **Soak tests:**
  - 72 hours of continuous recording
  - phone restart in the middle of a transfer
  - airplane mode for a day
  - a Railway restart in the middle of a job
- Cost dashboard: Scribe hours, OpenAI tokens, storage.
- Backups of the database (Railway snapshots), and a tested restore.

**Done when:** three days of real use pass with no lost audio, no surprise
deletions and no stuck items, and every failure on the way showed a recovery
path.

## Working rules for the build

- Small pull requests, one feature at a time, each linked to its milestone.
- Every external call (Plaud, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Drive) sits behind an
  interface with a fake for tests.
- Test on the real phone and recorder at the end of every milestone, not
  just in the emulator.
- Sample data in code and screenshots stays sample data. Real recordings
  never go in the repo.
- Update `docs/` whenever a decision changes.
